subtitle: When Patan Burned and Gujarat Refused to Die

panels.shot: epic split-scene wide, one half in flames, the other in rebuilding
panels.action: On one side, Bhima II stands small against a burning skyline of Patan; on the other, Lavanaprasada oversees masons raising new walls over blackened ruins, the same city scarred yet stirring back to life.

dialogue.text: In 1197 Qutb al-Din Aibak sacked Anhilwara-Patan—but under Bhima II and his Vaghela lords, the fallen capital rose again, and Gujarat refused to die.

i18n.hi: ११९७ में कुतुब अल-दीन ऐबक ने अन्हिलवाड़ा-पाटन लूटा, पर भीम द्वितीय और उनके वाघेला सरदारों के सहारे गिरी राजधानी फिर उठ खड़ी हुई, और गुजरात ने मरने से इंकार किया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a framed mural of a past battle
panels.action: A carved panel in a temple hall shows an older victory: Solanki warriors turning back a northern army in 1178, while a young Bhima II is depicted in miniature at the edge, watching history he did not make.

dialogue.text: Two dates haunt Gujarat: 1178, when Solankis threw back a Ghurid raid, and 1197, when Qutb al-Din Aibak came again and this time broke Anhilwara-Patan.

i18n.hi: दो तारीखें गुजरात को सताती हैं: ११७८, जब सोलंकीयों ने ग़ुरी हमले को धकेला, और ११९७, जब कुतुब अल-दीन ऐबक फिर आया और इस बार अन्हिलवाड़ा-पाटन को तोड़ गया।

panels.shot: high, distant bird’s-eye over western India
panels.action: A sweeping view of western India shows the dusty road from Delhi curving toward Patan, frontier forts like beads on a string, and beyond them the fertile plains and temples of Gujarat.

dialogue.text: By the 1190s, the Ghurid empire of Muhammad of Ghor and his slave-generals pressed west from Delhi, while Solanki Gujarat stood rich, tempting and exposed.

i18n.hi: ११९० के दशक तक, मुहम्मद ग़ौरी और उसके गुलाम-सैनापतियों का ग़ुरी साम्राज्य दिल्ली से पश्चिम की ओर दबा रहा था, जबकि सोलंकी गुजरात अमीर, ललचाने वाला और खुला पड़ा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of young Bhima II in court, slightly off-centre
panels.action: Bhima II, youthful and slight, sits on the Solanki throne in Patan’s pillared hall, while powerful nobles stand in clusters, leaning toward one another, their eyes measuring the king and each other.

dialogue.text: Bhima II inherited a throne ringed by ambitious feudatories—Paramaras and Yadavas at the borders, Vaghelas at his side, and Delhi’s new sultans beyond the horizon.

i18n.hi: भीम द्वितीय ने ऐसा सिंहासन संभाला जिसे महत्वाकांक्षी सामंतों ने घेर रखा था—सीमाओं पर परमार और यादव, बगल में वाघेला, और क्षितिज के पार दिल्ली के नए सुल्तान।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a marching army leaving Patan’s gate
panels.action: A disciplined Ghurid column with tall standards and mailed horsemen rides through a northern gateway, Qutb al-Din Aibak at its head, while in the far distance the outline of Patan shimmers in heat.

dialogue.text: In Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Minhaj-i-Siraj records Qutb al-Din Aibak riding west, capturing Nahrwala—Anhilwara-Patan—from Bhima’s forces in 1197.

i18n.hi: तबकात-ए-नासिरी में मिनहाज-ए-सिराज लिखते हैं कि ११९७ में कुतुब अल-दीन ऐबक पश्चिम आया और भीम की फौजों से नहरवाला—अन्हिलवाड़ा-पाटन—छीन लिया।

panels.shot: chaotic mid-range street-level view inside Patan during assault
panels.action: From within Patan’s streets, defenders scramble behind makeshift barricades as Ghurid soldiers pour through a breached gate, towers of the city’s temples rising in the background under a sky darkened by smoke.

dialogue.text: The Delhi army forced its way into the capital. Solanki resistance broke, and Anhilwara, which had once repelled Ghurids, now lay open to them.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली की सेना जबरन राजधानी में घुस गई। सोलंकी प्रतिरोध टूट गया, और अन्हिलवाड़ा, जिसने कभी ग़ुरीयों को रोका था, अब उनके लिए खुला पड़ा था।

panels.shot: somber wide across the skyline of Patan in flames
panels.action: The city’s silhouette—temple shikharas, mansions and markets—is wreathed in smoke as fires burn; statues topple from high towers, and people are driven in lines under armed guards toward the outskirts.

dialogue.text: Minhaj writes that Aibak’s men looted Anhilwara, damaged and destroyed temples, killed many and took others captive. Tradition remembers wealth carried off, and people marched away in chains.

i18n.hi: मिनहाज लिखते हैं कि ऐबक के सिपाहियों ने अन्हिलवाड़ा को लूटा, मंदिरों को तोड़ा-मरोड़ा, कईयों को मारा और कईयों को कैद कर ले गए। परंपरा याद रखती है लूटी दौलत और जंजीरों में बाँधकर ले जाए गए लोग।

panels.shot: tight, intimate shot inside a darkened, makeshift camp
panels.action: Bhima II sits in a dim camp outside the ruined capital, his face drawn, a lone lamp between him and Lavanaprasada, who leans over a rough map, his hand firm and eyes intense.

dialogue.text: “Maharaja, Patan is lost for now,” Lavanaprasada says, “but Gujarat is not.”

i18n.hi: “महाराज, अभी के लिए पाटन हाथ से गया है,” लवणप्रसाद कहते हैं, “पर गुजरात नहीं।”

panels.shot: medium close-up of Lavanaprasada addressing a circle of chiefs
panels.action: Lavanaprasada stands in armor before gathered local chiefs in a rural stronghold, pointing toward the direction of Patan; their faces show anger, doubt and a glimmer of resolve.

dialogue.text: Among Bhima’s feudatories, the Vaghela brothers Lavanaprasada and Shridhara moved to the forefront, marshalling scattered forces and calling local chiefs to a slow, stubborn counter-attack.

i18n.hi: भीम के सामंतों में वाघेला भाई लवणप्रसाद और श्रीधर आगे आए, बिखरी फौजों को समेटते हुए और देसी सरदारों को धीमी, जिद्दी जवाबी लड़ाई के लिए बुलाते हुए।

panels.shot: dynamic medium shot of Vaghela-led troops ambushing a small Ghurid detachment
panels.action: In a rugged countryside with scrub and rocky outcrops, Lavanaprasada leads a charge down a slope, catching a smaller, isolated band of Ghurid horsemen off guard as they ride with laden pack animals.

dialogue.text: The Ghurid garrison could not sit everywhere. Vaghela-led bands struck where the invaders were thin: supply lines, foraging parties, lightly held outposts in the hinterland.

i18n.hi: ग़ुरी फौज हर जगह डेरा नहीं डाल सकती थी। वाघेला-नेतृत्व वाले दले वहाँ चोट करते जहाँ घुसपैठिए कमज़ोर थे—रसद की राहें, चारा ढूँढती टुकड़ियाँ, अंदरूनी इलाकों में हल्के किले।

panels.shot: wide shot of a half-ruined Patan with returning Gujaratis entering cautiously
panels.action: Through a shattered gate, Lavanaprasada and Shridhara ride into Patan with their men; around them, townsfolk emerge from hiding, some weeping, some clasping hands in wary relief amid scorched walls.

dialogue.text: By around 1201, the Vaghelas had retaken Anhilwara-Patan. The Solanki capital, sacked but not erased, fell back under Bhima II’s name—and Vaghela protection.

i18n.hi: लगभग १२०१ तक वाघेलाओं ने अन्हिलवाड़ा-पाटन फिर ले लिया। सोलंकी राजधानी, जो लुटी पर मिटाई नहीं गई थी, भीम द्वितीय के नाम पर—और वाघेला की ढाल में—वापस आई।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Bhima II on a restored throne with Lavanaprasada beside
panels.action: Bhima II sits once more on the gilded throne in Patan, but this time Lavanaprasada stands at his right hand, slightly forward, receiving petitions from courtiers who bow first to the king, then glance toward the Vaghela lord.

dialogue.text: In inscriptions, Bhima remained maharajadhiraja. Yet, Dabhoi copper plates show grants issued under Lavanaprasada’s authority—the Vaghela power now anchored in royal ritual.

i18n.hi: शिलालेखों में भीम अब भी महाराजाधिराज रहे। पर डभोई की ताम्रपट्टियाँ दिखाती हैं कि दानपत्र लवणप्रसाद के अधिकार से जारी हुए—राजशाही अनुष्ठान में अब वाघेला शक्ति जमी हुई थी।

panels.shot: map-table overhead shot with hands placing tokens
panels.action: Around a large map, Bhima II, Lavanaprasada, and advisors place small wooden pieces marking hostile fronts: one toward the Paramaras of Malwa, another toward the Yadavas of the Deccan, and a third toward the northern frontier.

dialogue.text: Bhima’s troubles did not end with Patan’s recovery. Paramara and Yadava incursions, internal revolts, and the looming sultanate all pressed on Gujarat’s weakened rim.

i18n.hi: पाटन लौटने के बाद भी भीम की मुसीबतें खत्म नहीं हुईं। परमार और यादव घुसपैठ, अंदरूनी बगावतें और उभरती सल्तनत—सब मिलकर गुजरात की कमजोर सीमाओं पर चढ़ बैठे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a border skirmish with distant fort on a hill
panels.action: On a rocky frontier hill, Vaghela-led soldiers face an attacking force flying the emblem of a neighboring kingdom; Lavanaprasada signals a defensive formation while flames from a torched border village glow in the valley below.

dialogue.text: The kingdom ‘limped on,’ as later historians say. Victories were local and costly; forts were defended, villages sometimes lost, alliances constantly renegotiated.

i18n.hi: जैसा बाद के इतिहासकार लिखते हैं, यह राज्य ‘लड़खड़ाते हुए’ चला। जीतें स्थानीय और महँगी थीं; किले बचे रहे, गाँव कभी-कभी खो गए, और गठबंधन लगातार बदलते रहे।

panels.shot: interior close-up of a copper plate being inscribed
panels.action: A scribe incises letters onto a shining copper plate, while Lavanaprasada sits nearby with a calm, controlled expression, and Bhima II’s name is carefully etched in the formal opening lines.

dialogue.text: Vaghela records from Dabhoi and elsewhere praise Lavanaprasada as protector and commander, yet they open in Bhima’s name—testimony to a slow, layered transfer of real power.

i18n.hi: डभोई और अन्य जगहों के वाघेला लेख लवणप्रसाद को रक्षक और सेनापति कहकर सराहते हैं, पर शुरूआत भीम के नाम से करते हैं—धीमे, परतदार सत्ता-परिवर्तन की गवाही।

panels.shot: wide shot of craftsmen rebuilding a temple beside a still-ruined structure
panels.action: Artisans work carefully to repair a damaged temple mandapa, scaffolding around its cracked pillars, while beside it another shrine remains broken, its sanctum empty and open to the sky as worshippers light lamps at a temporary shrine.

dialogue.text: Not every sacred tower rose again. Some temples were rebuilt, others remained broken. The city lived amid its own scars, its rituals continuing in makeshift sanctuaries and restored halls alike.

i18n.hi: हर पवित्र शिखर फिर नहीं उठा। कुछ मंदिर बने, कुछ टूटे ही रहे। शहर अपने ही घावों के बीच जीता रहा, उसके अनुष्ठान अस्थायी देवालयों और फिर सजे मांडपों दोनों में चलते रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot of aging Bhima II and mature Lavanaprasada in quiet audience
panels.action: An older Bhima II sits more withdrawn on the throne, his shoulders slumped, while Lavanaprasada, now solid and composed, receives a delegation of provincial chiefs kneeling before him within the same hall.

dialogue.text: Over three decades after 1197, Bhima II’s line still formally ruled, but Vaghelas steered the state. Their rise was not a single coup; it was a long habit made visible.

i18n.hi: ११९७ के तीन दशक बाद भी भीम द्वितीय की वंश-रेखा कागज़ पर राज कर रही थी, पर राजकाज वाघेला चला रहे थे। उनका उभार किसी एक तख्तापलट से नहीं, बल्कि लंबी आदत के अचानक साफ दिखने से था।

panels.shot: dusk skyline of Patan with both figures in silhouette on a terrace
panels.action: At dusk, Bhima II and Lavanaprasada stand together on a terrace overlooking Patan; the city spreads below with both restored and ruined structures, torches flickering as night approaches.

dialogue.text: Cynthia Talbot and others note that Gujarat did not fall with the sack of 1197. Instead, it adapted—its kings diminished, its feudatories ascendant, its capital battered but functioning.

i18n.hi: सिंथिया टैलबॉट और अन्य इतिहासकार नोट करते हैं कि ११९७ की लूट से गुजरात नहीं गिरा। उसने रूप बदला—राजा छोटे हुए, सामंत ऊँचे, राजधानी घायल रही पर चलती रही।

panels.shot: close, contemplative shot of Lavanaprasada’s and Bhima’s profiles, side by side
panels.action: In a quiet interior lit by a single oil lamp, the profiles of Bhima II and Lavanaprasada are seen in partial shadow, the flame between them, throwing shifting light on their contrasting expressions of weariness and resolve.

dialogue.text: Between Aibak’s sack and the later Vaghela takeover, Bhima II’s Gujarat shows another kind of heroism: a kingdom that survived half-broken, half-usurped, yet alive—and a reminder that not all resistance ends in clean victory or simple fall.

i18n.hi: ऐबक की लूट और बाद के वाघेला कब्जे के बीच का भीम द्वितीय का गुजरात बहादुरी की दूसरी तस्वीर है: एक ऐसा राज्य जो आधा टूटा, आधा हथिया लिया गया, फिर भी जिंदा रहा—और याद दिलाता रहा कि हर प्रतिरोध सुथरी जीत या साफ हार पर खत्म नहीं होता।
